attempted_claim: Let Gamma be a centrally symmetric C^6 strictly convex closed planar curve, not assumed to be an ellipse. Prove or disprove: if its billiard map simultaneously possesses a smooth convex rational caustic of rotation number exactly 1/4 consisting entirely of 4-periodic orbits and a smooth convex rational caustic of rotation number exactly 1/6 consisting entirely of 6-periodic orbits, then Gamma must be an ellipse. A complete answer is either a rigorous rigidity proof deriving ellipseness from coexistence of the 1/4 and 1/6 rational caustics under central symmetry via Bialy-Mironov generating-function and mirror-curvature integral constraints, or an explicit centrally symmetric C^6 non-ellipse table certified to carry both exact rational caustics.
decisive_failure: value: Headline is finite-order flattening of the frozen equal-spaced q-gon range, explicitly necessary but not sufficient for a true smooth rational caustic (needs pinned-minimal perimeter, reflection law, smoothness, all-orders convergence). It is neither a rigidity proof nor a certified coexistence table. The q|k rule restates standard linear theory; the -1/4 coefficient is a fitted proxy parameter for modes 20/40 vs 30/60 at k=10 with only a numerically tiny proxy-residual improvement and no demonstrated downstream use for true 1/4+1/6 caustics. Under STANDARD this is a textbook restatement plus parameter fit on an artificial object, not an independently retrievable exact invariant of a natural object.
